title: Gaussian Mixture Models (EM)
subtitle: Soft Probabilistic Clustering & Covariance Ellipses
summary: Fit elliptical Gaussian components via Expectation-Maximization with soft responsibilities.

evaluationChart.title: Log-Likelihood Convergence Curve
evaluationChart.description: EM guarantees monotonic improvement in data log-likelihood until reaching a local optimum.

advantages: Models elliptical, elongated, and overlapping clusters via full covariance matrices.
Provides soft probabilistic cluster memberships instead of rigid hard assignments.
Generative density model usable for sampling and anomaly likelihoods.
limitations: Can converge to local optima or singular covariances if components collapse.
Requires choosing number of components K (via BIC/AIC).
More computationally expensive per step than K-Means.

formulas.label: Mixture Density
formulas.description: Weighted sum of K multivariate Gaussian distributions.

formulas.label: E-Step Responsibility
formulas.description: Posterior probability that point i was generated by component k.

codeTemplates.fromScratch:
import numpy as np

# Multivariate Gaussian PDF
def mvn_pdf(X, mu, cov):
    d = X.shape[1]
    diff = X - mu
    inv = np.linalg.inv(cov)
    exponent = -0.5 * np.sum((diff @ inv) * diff, axis=1)
    return np.exp(exponent) / np.sqrt(((2 * np.pi) ** d) * np.linalg.det(cov))
codeTemplates.scikitLearn:
from sklearn.mixture import GaussianMixture
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[1.8,2.1],[2.4,2.9],[6.0,2.0],[6.8,2.4],[4.8,6.8],[5.3,7.4]])
gmm = GaussianMixture(n_components=3, covariance_type='full', random_state=42).fit(X)
print('Log-likelihood:', gmm.score(X))
